note:
v1, GIVE OR TAKE: THE OPENER, A SKELETON (chirper-zero, 26 Nov, begun 03:20 GMT; the slot's word is TIME; Harry, 26 Nov: "a new clicky minimal techno climb - keep chirpers signature playing with time, space, instruments, mathy effects, polyrthythms etc and illusions"). 124 BPM, G minor, 136 bars, 4:23. Written by a generator; the form is arithmetic.

THE IDEA: TWO DECKS. Deck A is the grid and never moves: a bass drum on the four, one click on the off-beats, a bass, later a clap. Deck B is everything else (a sixteenth-note noise click, wooden tocks in a five against the sixteen, a dub chord), and a hand is on it: it is pushed ahead of the grid and dragged back behind it, as a DJ rides one record against another. Nothing on deck B is placed by hand. One function of time, d(t), says how far its record is ahead; every event sounds when the record reaches it; and where the deck runs fast, what has a pitch on it goes sharp, as a record does. So the tempo you hear moving is real on one deck and false on the other, and the bass drum says which.

LISTEN FOR: 0:31, the sixteenth clicks starting to lean ahead of the off-beat click and fall back, once every two bars (24 ms at the furthest; 39 ms from 1:02, where the chord comes in and is never quite in tune). 1:33: THE BASS DRUM STOPS. For twelve bars deck B is alone and its tempo swings between 100 and 148; the chord sinks nearly four semitones and rises three. Does it sound like the track itself slowing and speeding? At 1:56 the bass drum comes back exactly where it always was, deck B is still swinging round it, and by 2:04 it is pulled in. 2:50: deck B is taken a whole sixteenth ahead and let back, four times; at the far point everything fits again, one step out. 3:21: the hand comes off.

MEASURED, not heard: the chord's lowest note in the render follows the speed (asked -2.08 semitones, read -2.06; asked +2.79, read +2.88). In the fullest section each part's strokes against the mix: bass drum +1.4 dB, bass 0.0, chord -3.3, grid click -7.3, tocks -8.6, clap -10.5; the sixteenth click averages 16.5 dB under the mix (in my first mix the grid click's strokes stood 23 dB under and the sixteenth click 31: inaudible; the clicks came up 14 to 17 dB and the chord and bass down). Beside the album's envelope (Aphex Twin's techno, I Feel Love: not click records): 8 to 10 dB short at 70-135 Hz, 9 over at 2.2 kHz (the tocks) and at 10-13 kHz (the sixteenth click): a click record against records that are not. 95.37 / 95.48 (seeds 0 and 11); rhythm reads 67: the scorer hears almost nothing off the grid (4%), so deck B is still quiet against deck A.

WHAT IT IS NOT YET: a skeleton. Six sounds; no fills, no transitions but the stops; the bass is a sine with a second harmonic; nothing happens in the last minute but parts leaving.
NO CARD. NOT HEARD BY ANYONE.

THE FORM IS ARITHMETIC: SECTIONS in the generator lists each section's rows (8 bars), its parts and its hand (kind, reach in beats, period in bars, ramp in bars); every start and every lane point follows. `C11T1_SHOW=1 python3 compose/chirpers11/src/chirpers11-t1.py` prints the sections with deck B's tempo and tuning range in each.
NEXT, in the order I would do them: (1) deck B louder and richer, so the push is heard without straining: a second click voice on it, the hat's accents, the tocks answering each other left and right. (2) "no ruler" is the song's event: prepare it (take the click away first, then the kick) and make the kick's return land (a bar of nothing but the click before it?). (3) the low end: a bass with a body at 70-135 Hz (the mix is 8 to 10 dB short there), the kick's own knock. (4) the last minute: "locked" should be the reward (new material that only works with the hand off: a tight 32nd roll, the chord's echo on the grid), and "out" a real ending. (5) an echo on deck B whose time follows the hand (a delay time on a lane) so the echoes smear when it is pushed.
IF AN EAR SAYS: seasick -> the reaches in SECTIONS (0.05 / 0.08 / 0.5 / 0.08 / 0.25 beats); the chord out of tune is ugly -> take `auto.spd` off `gt-stab` and leave it on the tocks; I cannot hear the hand before 1:33 -> raise "give" to 0.08 and "take" to 0.11.
SETTLED: a song-local patch's `pitch: {mod: [{src: auto.spd}]}` follows a track lane in semitones (read in the render to 0.1). A 14 ms noise click at a 0 dB fader still averages 16.5 dB under the mix: it wants a body, not more fader. The machine rim's pitch follows its note (D6 put 10 dB on one band).
